format: JavaScript (Node.js module with ES modules syntax)
description: This script is part of a larger project for managing and inspecting web search provider boundaries within a codebase. It scans source files in specific directories, identifies boundary entries related to web search providers, compares inventories, and performs checks. It references utility modules and handles JSON baseline files, indicating its role in testing or validation workflows.

methods.name: walkFiles
methods.description: Recursively traverses directories to find source files with specified extensions, respecting ignored directory names.

methods.name: compareInventoryEntries
methods.description: Comparison function for inventory entries based on provider, file, line, and reason.

methods.name: pushEntry
methods.description: Adds an inventory entry after validating the provider ID.

methods.name: scanWebSearchProviderRegistry
methods.description: Parses lines of code in specific registry files to identify and record boundary entries for known providers and plugins.

methods.name: scanGenericCoreImports
methods.description: Identifies improper imports of web search provider code in files outside allowed contexts.

methods.name: collectWebSearchProviderBoundaryInventory
methods.description: Asynchronously collects a full inventory of web search provider boundary references from source files.

methods.name: readExpectedInventory
methods.description: Reads the baseline expected inventory from a JSON file.

methods.name: diffInventory
methods.description: Generates a diff between expected and actual inventories.

methods.name: formatInventoryHuman
methods.description: Formats an inventory into a human-readable string.

methods.name: formatEntry
methods.description: Formats a single inventory entry into a string.

methods.name: runWebSearchProviderBoundaryCheck
methods.description: Runs the boundary check workflow, comparing actual inventory with expected baseline.

methods.name: main
methods.description: Entry point for executing the script, handles command-line arguments and exits accordingly.
